ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Emily Dickinson — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Video visit four weeks after the losartan increase and dapagliflozin start, with home vital signs and home blood tests

text.paragraph: Video visit four weeks after the losartan increase and dapagliflozin start. [S]

Ms. Dickinson is seen by video from her home. The mobile phlebotomy service drew her blood this morning. Before the call she measured her blood pressure twice with her validated upper-arm cuff after five minutes' rest, and her weight, temperature, and oxygen saturation with her own devices; Dr. Hartwell counted her breathing on video. She has taken losartan 100 mg and dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for four weeks. She has had a headache only once in the past two weeks. She passes a little more urine and has had no lightheadedness, genital itching, or urinary symptoms. Her home blood pressure averages 138/84 over the past two weeks. She drinks to thirst, about 1.5 L a day. [S]

list.item:
Chronic kidney disease G3a A2 (N18.31). Four weeks after increasing losartan and starting dapagliflozin, creatinine 1.32 mg/dL (eGFR 48) and potassium 4.8 mmol/L. The creatinine has risen about 10 percent from baseline, the expected early dip with these drugs and well within the 30 percent that is accepted. [S]
Continue losartan 100 mg and dapagliflozin 10 mg.
Urine albumin-creatinine ratio and metabolic panel at the three-month review.
Sick-day rules reviewed again.

Hypertension with chronic kidney disease (I12.9). 136/84 mmHg on her home cuff today and 138/84 on average, still above the KDIGO systolic target of below 120 on a maximum-dose ARB. [S]
Start amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Report ankle swelling or lightheadedness.
Send home readings weekly.
